title: # Reality Fracture prerelease cheat sheet (DEC-925)
intro: Grades are Sealed grades, 0 to 10, from oracle text (CEO, 2026-09-23), cross-checked against Draftsim. ★ bomb, ✕ removal, ⚡ trick or instant-speed interaction, ◆ fixing. A grade in parentheses applies when your deck holds the listed number of enablers.
procedure_splash: 5. If a third color holds a card graded 7 or higher, splash it only with 2 or more lands in the pool that make that color: a dual land (common Annex/Commons or rare slowland) or Room of Refuge. Murmuring Volume and the basic landcyclers (Hexhaven Battalion, Undulating Witness, Apex Witchstalker, Awaken the Inferno, Vinelasher Adept) help the splash but do not count toward the 2. Splash at most 2 cards.
procedure_tiebreak: 7. If two pairs tie, prefer the one with more 6-or-higher cards, then the one whose synergy grades turn on (Jace count, graveyard count, lifegain count), then the one with more 2-drops.
removal_lead: Count and quality by colour (mono-colour cards only; ✕ role). White has fewer removal cards than black or red but its commons and uncommons are the best-graded; red has the most at common, which is what a 40-common pool actually opens.
ranking_heading: ## 5. Archetype ranking (Monte Carlo over the booster collation, DEC-926)
ranking_commentary: Read this as "what the set makes likely", not as a pick: mean scores sit within 0.15 of each other, so the pool you open decides. Read P(best) as tiers, not an order: a one-point change on a dozen grades moved pairs by up to 2 points in review. Tier 1: WB. Tier 2: BR, WG, UB, UR, WU, WR. Tier 3: BG, UG, RG. Stable across every model version: white pairs have the highest P(viable), UG and WU the lowest, RG the lowest P(best).
ranking_reading: **How to read it at the table.** White pairs top P(viable) because white has the most playables and its removal is premium (Memory Trap, Prophesied End, Your Fate Ends Here are all grade 7) but few: 5 white removal cards at common and uncommon against 6 red and 7 black. Red and black have the most removal by count, so BR decks average about 6 removal spells and white pairs 4 to 6. Blue pairs are removal-poor (UG and WU lowest). A pool that opens 3 or more black or red removal spells is usually a BR/WB/WR deck; a pool with a white bomb and lifegain is WG. Green is the least likely main colour, not a bad one.
